title: Cathode / neutralizer evidence dossier for an air-breathing Hall system (published / open evidence only)
status: EVIDENCE DOSSIER ONLY. No simulator parameter, threshold, frozen dataset, chemistry table or campaign file is changed by this file. It is not a design input until the owner decides so.
companion: docs/evidence/cathode/CATHODE_DOSSIER.md (human-readable summary; this JSON is authoritative)

policy.evidence_rules: docs/EVIDENCE.md and CLAUDE.md rules 6 and 10. Evidence level (1-7) describes the source; quantity_type describes what happened to the number. They are orthogonal.
policy.level_assignment_in_this_dossier: No Vyovrinda cathode exists, so no entry is level 1 or 2. Level 3 = primary experimental report on hardware of the same cathode concept (transfer to Vyovrinda hardware is an applicability limitation, not a level change). Level 5 = textbook, review, or a value quoted by a paper from another primary that this lane did not retrieve, or a value known only from a document title. Level 7 = repository constant with no located source.

policy.numbers_not_entered: Numbers seen only in search-engine result summaries (not in a retrieved document or title) are NOT entered as values; the studies are listed under leads_not_entered with what must be read.
policy.access_rules_followed: Published / openly accessible sources only. Pages that returned a paywall, a login redirect, a bot challenge or a human-verification page were not bypassed and are recorded as not retrieved. No person or lab was contacted. LXCat not used.
policy.retrieved_files_not_committed: Source PDFs were read from a scratch directory and are not redistributed; their sha256 is recorded so the exact file read can be re-identified.

baseline_decision.statement: The system baseline stays a Xe-fed hollow cathode (thermionic; LaB6 or BaO-W emitter). Atmospheric-gas-fed cathode operation (air, N2, O2, or a subset of the intake flow) is UNRESOLVED for the RFP use case: no retrieved source demonstrates a thermionic hollow cathode operating on air/N2/O2, and the air-fed plasma cathodes that have been demonstrated (microwave AMPCAT, RF NewOrbit) are at <= 0.9 A, with continuous operation reported only up to 2 h (AMPCAT) and no life test, versus a Hall cathode that must carry the full discharge current I_d (TBD) for > 15,000 h of firing.
baseline_decision.does_not_claim: This dossier does not claim ABEP closure, an architecture winner, a cathode selection, or any Hall transport admission. It does not propose retuning any model.

rfp_envelope_as_quoted.note: Quoted from the CLAUDE.md transcription of RFP DTDF/06/13516/DSP/ABEP/X/L/M/01. The RFP document itself is not in the repository; verify against the RFP before quoting externally. These are requirements, not evidence, and are kept as text.

principle.claim: The hollow cathode in a Hall thruster provides electrons for both ionization of the propellant gas and neutralization of the beam; Hall thrusters need higher cathode currents than ion thrusters at the same power because they run at lower Isp.
principle.note: Qualitative textbook statement; quantity_type 'measured' refers to the underlying thruster practice it summarizes.

principle.claim: Neutralizer cathodes in ion thrusters emit electrons at a current equal to the beam current (for context: a gridded architecture would size the neutralizer on I_b, a Hall architecture sizes the cathode on I_d).

When a keeper is run in steady state, the cathode's total emission current is the keeper current plus the thruster current it supplies (NEXT neutralizer: total emission = keeper current + beam current).

symbolic_relations: E1  I_emit = I_d + I_k   (I_k = steady keeper current; I_k = 0 if the keeper is switched off after ignition). For a Hall thruster the cathode supplies I_d = I_b + I_e,channel.

E3  P_d = eta_PPU,anode * (P_EP,max - sum_j P_aux,j / eta_PPU,j),  with P_EP,max bounded by the RFP '< 1.5 kW' (definition of what the 1.5 kW covers: TBD against the RFP text) and P_aux,j = magnets, cathode heater and keeper, compressor, other loads.
E4  I_b = eta_b * I_d  (current utilization)  =>  I_d = I_b / eta_b
E5  I_emit,max = max over the operating envelope of (P_d / V_d) + I_k;  I_emit,min = min over the envelope (sets the low-current flow-margin / plume-mode limit).

E6  m_Xe,cathode = mdot_c * t_fire,  t_fire > 15,000 h (RFP), plus start-up and conditioning flow; mdot_c chosen for spot-mode margin at I_emit,min (flow margin shrinks with orifice erosion, see herman_2009_next_neutralizer).
E7  Air-fed plasma cathode (if ever pursued): mdot_c,air = M_eff * I_emit / (e * U_i) and P_c = I_emit / C_e, with U_i and C_e defined as in tisaev_2024_ampcat Eq. (1).

E8  Thermionic emitter: J = I_emit / A_emit;  J = A_R * T^2 * exp(-e*phi / (k*T)) with phi = phi(T, coverage); coverage depends on p_O,emitter = f_shield * p_O,local (f_shield: no located source; TBD).
E9  Cathode life requirement: t_life,cathode >= t_fire (> 15,000 h) * qualification margin (margin TBD); ignition cycles N_ign >= mission firing schedule (TBD).

numeric_evaluation.tbd: TBD - requires (a) Vyovrinda V_d and P_d at the RFP operating points, which need either an admitted Hall transport closure (gate 3 is FAIL; the credible closure set is empty; all absolute Hall numbers are withdrawn) or Vyovrinda hardware measurements; (b) the PPU efficiency and auxiliary power allocation inside the 1.5 kW cap; (c) the steady keeper policy (I_k). No numeric I_d is derived here from thrust, because that would require a Hall closure that does not exist.

candidates.name: Xe-fed LaB6 hollow cathode (thermionic, bulk emitter)
candidates.summary: Bulk emitter; tolerates about two orders of magnitude more O2/H2O impurity than BaO-W at equal emission current density (textbook statement from diode tests); runs hotter (about 1600 degC class). Hall-thruster flight heritage with LaB6 cathodes is reported (Russian SPT family). Life basis is a model plus one title-level 13,011 h demonstration for a heaterless sub-kW Hall cathode (body not retrieved).

recovery_cleaning.claim: LaB6 cathodes do not require any significant conditioning or activation procedure (unlike dispenser cathodes); after atmospheric air or water-vapour exposure they restarted normally after pump-out and reheating.

Raising emitter temperature is the stated mitigation against oxide poisoning in O2-bearing plasma (lanthanum-oxide formation avoided at just over 1600 degC in 1e-3 Torr O2). The cost is higher evaporation (life) and heater/keeper power; the trade is not quantified in the retrieved sources.

recovery_cleaning.claim: A cathode conditioning procedure was applied whenever atmospheric exposure was suspected; dispenser cathodes need conditioning/activation procedures that LaB6 does not.
recovery_cleaning.note: Second half of the claim: goebel_katz_2008_ch6 book p. 306.

recovery_cleaning.claim: Barium recycling in the insert plasma reduced the effective evaporation rate and extended NSTAR cathode life beyond the depletion model; about 30 % of the original barium remained after the ELT.

The 27,800 h cathode failed during a restart attempt; destructive analysis found two forms of barium tungstate (a Ba-Ca tungstate whose formula is garbled in the scanned text, and BaWO4) over a majority of the emitter surface and tungsten deposition near the orifice; the insert state was consistent with expected impregnate chemistry (end of usable life).

uncertainty_register.item: LaB6 O2 tolerance statements under different conditions
uncertainty_register.description: Textbook: LaB6 ran in 1e-3 Torr O2 background at > 1600 degC and tolerates 1e-4 Torr O2 at 1570 degC; AMPCAT paper: current density drops at about 1e-3 mbar air; AETHER (secondary): up to 12 % air in the Xe feed caused sparking and erosion. Different geometries (diode, plasma source, hollow cathode with internal pressure > 1 Torr) and gases (O2 vs air); not contradictory but not reconcilable without primaries.
